module.title: Commercial and financial inputs for contract preparation

slides.title: What you will be able to do
objectives: Identify key principles and best practices in exclusive contract negotiation and transaction support
Identify commercial and financial inputs required for contract preparation

slides.title: Procurement process and entry to negotiation

media.placeholder: Flowchart: Market Engagement → RFQ → RFP → Negotiations & Project Agreements (negotiation stage highlighted)

bullets: RFP evaluation leads to selection of a preferred proponent
Preferred proponent enters exclusive negotiation — sole right to negotiate project agreement terms
This module focuses on what happens at this stage — preparing commercial and financial inputs for contract documentation

slides.title: From inputs to close

media.placeholder: Diagram: commercial inputs → commercial close documents (left); financial inputs → financial close documents (right)

bullets: Commercial close: Project Agreement, construction contract, services contract, letters of credit, performance security
Financial close: adapted PA to Project Co.'s structure, alignment across project documents, price adjustment for market movements
Key factors: timing, payment structures, alignment between documents

slides.title: Commercial inputs
body: - What: contract types (fixed-price, cost-reimbursable, T&M, design-build, PPP); key contractual terms and conditions (scope, payment, change management, performance standards, termination, dispute resolution)
- Where from: procurement and transaction development; contract-development work
- Who contributes: Technical Advisors, Financial Advisors, Legal Advisors, Procurement Authority, Transaction Process Advisors
- Why they matter: they shape the contractual structure and terms to be finalized at close
slides.key_message: Commercial inputs define HOW the deal is structured — contract type, terms, and risk allocation.

slides.title: Financial inputs
body: - What: Financial Plan / Financial Offering; Financing / Funding Plan; Financial Modelling; Price Form(s)
- Where from: financial submission requirements; financial analysis supporting project and procurement decisions
- Who contributes: Financial Advisors and related project / advisory roles
- Why they matter: they support financial suitability, value-for-money analysis, pricing, and funding structure
slides.key_message: Financial inputs determine WHETHER the deal is viable — funding, pricing, and value for money.

slides.title: How inputs map to close documents

media.placeholder: Visual: left column shows commercial inputs flowing into commercial close docs; right column shows financial inputs flowing into financial close docs

bullets: Commercial inputs produce: Project Agreement, construction contract, services contract, letters of credit, performance security
Financial inputs produce: adapted PA to Project Co.'s structure, aligned project documents, price adjustment reflecting market movements
Both must align — timing, payment structures, and document consistency are where gaps appear

slides.title: Practice
slides.stem: Which sequence best reflects the transition into negotiation and project agreement finalization in a public sector procurement process?
options: Market engagement → RFQ → RFP → negotiations and project agreements
RFQ → contract management → market engagement → financial close
Bid evaluation → contract closeout → RFP → RFQ
Packaging analysis → supplier onboarding → dispute resolution → financial modelling
slides.feedback_correct: Correct. The standard public sector procurement sequence moves from market engagement through RFQ and RFP stages before entering negotiations and project agreement finalization.
slides.feedback_incorrect: The correct sequence is: market engagement → RFQ → RFP → negotiations and project agreements. Each stage builds on the previous one.

slides.title: Practice
slides.stem: Which set of inputs is most directly associated with contract preparation?
options: Funding structure, financial model inputs, price forms, payment terms, and contract-related assumptions
Community feedback, maintenance logs, variation history, and closeout reports
Bidder interview notes, shortlist rankings, and debrief letters
KPI scorecards, claims registers, and handover certificates
slides.feedback_correct: Correct. These inputs — funding structure, financial models, price forms, payment terms, and contract assumptions — are the core financial and commercial inputs needed for contract preparation.
slides.feedback_incorrect: The correct answer is A. Funding structure, financial models, price forms, and payment terms are directly used in contract preparation. The other options relate to different stages of the procurement or contract lifecycle.

slides.title: Knowledge check
slides.stem: A project team has completed bidder evaluation and selected a preferred proponent. The team now needs to move into the next stage of the transaction. What should they focus on first?
options: Launch performance reporting and KPI reviews
Finalize project agreement terms and close-related documentation
Begin dispute resolution planning for post-award issues
Re-open RFQ shortlisting to validate market capacity
slides.feedback_correct: Correct. Once a preferred proponent is selected, the next focus is negotiation and project agreement finalization, including commercial and financial close documentation.
slides.feedback_incorrect: The correct answer is B. After selecting a preferred proponent, the team should finalize project agreement terms and close-related documentation. Performance reporting (A) belongs to contract management after delivery begins. Dispute resolution (C) is a later contract-lifecycle concern. Re-opening RFQ (D) occurs earlier in the process.

slides.title: Knowledge check
slides.stem: The team is preparing contract documentation after selecting the preferred proponent. Technical inputs are available, but key commercial and financial inputs are incomplete. What should the team obtain next?
options: Contract terms/structures plus funding-plan, model, and price-form inputs
Dispute-board procedures and live claims records
slides.feedback_correct: Correct. Contract preparation depends on contract-related commercial positions and financial inputs that shape the agreement and close documentation.
slides.feedback_incorrect: The correct answer is B. Contract preparation requires commercial inputs (contract terms and structures) and financial inputs (funding plan, model, price forms). Closeout reports (A) happen at end of contract lifecycle. Performance dashboards (C) belong to contract management after award. Dispute records (D) are later contract-administration issues.

slides.title: Key takeaways
takeaways: Exclusive negotiation follows preferred proponent selection — the team finalizes project agreement terms through commercial close and financial close
Contract preparation requires two categories of inputs: commercial (contract types, terms, conditions) and financial (funding plan, financial model, price forms) — both must align for close
